# The Method for the Gift of a Ram as Taught by Dhaumya

### The gift of a ram to please Ketu during the major period of Jupiter and the sub-period of Ketu. When Ketu is in the sub-period of Jupiter, if it is joined with or aspected by malefics, situated in a cruel planetary division (*krūragraha-aṃśa*), or placed in a house of affliction, then during its sub-period, there will be strife with the king and the loss of wealth. It likewise causes dizziness, headaches, abdominal colic, and other such ailments. It bestows the fruits of past actions such as jaundice, anemia, or poisonous diseases. To remedy these defects, one should perform the worship of the Shiva Linga. One should also perform the gift of a ram; by this, one undoubtedly attains peace. **According to the *Karma Vipāka*:** The procedure for the ritual gift of a living ram—one who desires to perform this gift, during auspicious times such as the *ayanas*, in temples, or in holy places, should prepare a portion of ground smeared with cow-dung and decorated with *raṅgavalli* (ritual designs). Having placed a young ram facing the east, one should adorn its horns with gold, its hooves with silver, and its tail with pearls. It should be wrapped in a silken cloth. ---

### The gift of Lakshmi-Narayana to please Venus during the major period of Jupiter and the sub-period of Venus. When Venus is in the sub-period of Jupiter, if it is in its sign of debilitation, combust (*maudhya*), defeated in planetary war, joined with malefics, or situated in the sixth, twelfth, or eighth house, then during its sub-period, there will be the loss of livestock and the wrath of the king. There will be suffering such as hemorrhaging or blood-related disorders, despite performing sacrificial acts. It also causes the loss of life, heart disease, and the fear of death. To remedy these defects, one should perform the gift of Lakshmi-Narayana according to the prescribed method; thereby one attains peace. The procedure is the same as for the sub-period of Mercury during the major period of the Moon. ---

### The gift of a goat to please the Sun during the major period of Jupiter and the sub-period of the Sun. ### PHYSICS, BOOK VIII

to judge in the same way as those who are older, for the confusion and motion surrounding them are great. <note>original: "πολλὴ γὰρ ἡ ταραχὴ καὶ ἡ κίνησις"</note> One is established and settles into a state of rest—sometimes by nature itself, and at other times by other things—yet in both cases, some things within the body undergo alteration, just as in the case of waking and of activity, when one becomes sober and awakens. It is therefore evident from what has been said that being altered and <term>alteration</term> <gloss>a change in quality</gloss> take place in sensible things and in the sensitive part of the soul, and in nothing else except by accident.

One might puzzle over whether every motion is comparable to every other motion or not. If all are comparable, and if that which moves an equal amount in an equal time is of equal speed, then some curved line would be equal to a straight line, and furthermore, a greater one and a smaller one would be equal. Moreover, alteration and <term>locomotion</term> <gloss>motion in space</gloss> would be equal when, in an equal time, one thing is altered and the other is moved. Thus, a change in quality would be equal to a length. But this is impossible. Is it then the case that whenever something is moved by an equal amount in an equal time, it is of equal speed? But a change in quality is not equal to a length. Thus, there is no alteration equal to a locomotion, nor even a smaller one. Therefore, not everything is comparable. And how will it happen in the case of a circle and a straight line? For it is absurd if one cannot move in a circle in the same way as in a straight line, but there is an immediate necessity to move either faster or slower, just as if one were moving downhill and the other uphill. Furthermore, it makes no difference in the argument if someone claims that there is a necessity to move faster or slower immediately; for the curved line would be greater and smaller than the straight one, and consequently also equal. For if in time A, one thing 

<column-break/>

traversed B and the other traversed C, then B would be greater than C; for let it be said that this was the faster. It is no different if the same amount is traversed in less time, it is faster; thus there will be some part of A in which it traverses the equal amount of the circle, and in the whole of A it traverses C. However, if they are comparable, the result just mentioned occurs: that a straight line is equal to a circular one. But they are not comparable; therefore, neither are the motions. But all things that are not <term>homonymous</term> <gloss>having the same name but different definitions</gloss> are comparable. For example, why is it not comparable whether a stylus, wine, or the <term>nete</term> <gloss>the highest-pitched string of a lyre</gloss> is sharper? Because they are homonymous, they are not comparable; but the <term>nete</term> is comparable to the <term>paranete</term> <gloss>the string next to the highest</gloss>, because "sharp" signifies the same thing in both. Is it therefore not the same "fast" here and there? It is even less so in alteration and locomotion. Or is this first point—that non-homonymous things are comparable—not true? For "much" signifies the same thing in water and in air, yet they are not comparable. And if not that, "double" signifies the same (for it is two to one), and they are not comparable. Or is the same account true for these as well? For "much" is also homonymous. But in some cases, the definitions themselves are homonymous, as if one were to say that "much" is "that amount and something else." "That amount" and "equal" are homonymous, and even "one," as it happens, is immediately homonymous. If this is so, then "two" is also; for why are some things comparable and others not, if there were one nature? Or is it because they are in a different primary receptive subject? A horse and a dog are comparable as to which is whiter; for the subject in which it primarily resides—the surface—is the same. And the same applies to magnitude. But water and sound are not; for they are in different subjects. Or is it clear that in this way one could make everything one, in another...

אע"פ שעניינו לתרומה גדולה והכל אלו הדברים כי הם נפלאים

### וכבר הרי

<margin>
כי יכיננוא' בתיקונים סוד ברוך שהוא י"ת כד"ד דא"ש ומקד"ל כ"ל שלומד למקום קודש הש"ל

אמרתי כי במעשרות והברכות סוד אחד ומקום אחד וכו' כמו שכתב הרקנאטי ז"ל ובלאר חורור פנימי של עשירי בבינוי בברכה ח"ל וא' מבואר סוד מאה שערים וסוד ויברכהו ה' ולבאר חנינו עתיקין דבבי שעורי אורה בשער הראשון בבינוי בברכה ח"ל ויהי מאה אדנים שבמשכן הם בדמיון מאה ברכות המתמלאות מן הבריכה הגדולה הנקרא אדנ"י ולפיכך חייב אדם לברך מאה ברכות בכל יום כדי למשוך מכל אחת ואחת מאות הברכות ואם חסר אחת פגום ומטיל מום ויהיה חסר בכבור אלהים כדכתיב שח' סוד כהן לוי וישראל' שזהו סוד נפש רוח ונשמה ולפי עקר זה' אמר רח"ח בברכי נפשי את ה' תלוה הברכות בנפש בסוד שלשה המעשרות

# The Portion of Toledot - The Written Torah
## This is the name by which it shall be called: The Source of Blessings

### The Lamp of the Commandment

<margin>
"And Isaac sowed in that land and found in that year a hundredfold, and the Lord blessed him." <note>Genesis 26:12</note> The Midrash <note>Bereishit Rabbah</note> says, and Rashi brings in his commentary, that "a hundredfold" <note>original: *Me’ah Shearim*, literally "a hundred gates" or "a hundred measures"</note> means that they estimated how much the field was fit to produce, and it produced a hundred times more than the estimate. Our Sages of blessed memory said this estimation was for the purpose of tithes.
</margin>

Note that the Patriarchs fulfilled the entire Torah. The Torah detailed this quality in its specifics—commandments that were practiced, as we find with Abraham our Patriarch, who "gave a tithe of everything." <note>Genesis 14:20</note> We find the same here with Isaac, and likewise with Jacob, who said: "And of all that You give me, I will surely give a tenth to You." <note>Genesis 28:22</note> Jacob our Patriarch even gave a tithe from souls; our Sages explained that there were fourteen tribes counting Ephraim and Manasseh, and after subtracting the four firstborns of the matriarchs <note>who are inherently holy and belong to God</note>, ten remained, and Levi was set aside to be holy. Thus, the Patriarchs fulfilled the commandment of the tithe with all their heart, all their soul, and all their might. "Their might" is understood in its plain sense as a tithe from all their wealth, including a tithe of money. "With all their soul" refers to Jacob tithing the souls of his sons. "With all their heart" relates to the Great Offering <note>term: *Terumah Gedolah* — the portion of the harvest given to the Priest</note>, which has no fixed legal measure but depends entirely on the generosity of one's heart. Regarding this "offering of the Lord," our Sages said: a generous eye gives one-fortieth; an average eye, one-fiftieth; and a stingy eye, one-sixtieth. This is all hinted at in the verse "And he gave him a tithe of all." It would have been sufficient to say "he gave a tithe," but the phrase "of all" hints at the Great Offering, for the "tithe of the tithe" <note>given by the Levite to the Priest</note> is included within the general category of tithes, as I will explain later. For Abraham gave Melchizedek the tithe and also the Great Offering. Now, our Sages calculated that 50 is the "average eye" <note>1/50th</note>. But Abraham, being a man of kindness, took ten out of fifty so he could give the Great Offering from them; by removing ten from fifty, forty remained—meaning he gave one part out of forty for the Great Offering. Even though the average way is one out of fifty, he removed ten from fifty and then set aside one for the Great Offering because he was generous of heart, like all the Patriarchs. Regarding the Great Offering, it seems we can resolve the statement "this estimation was for tithes." A difficulty arises: does the Mishnah not rule, "Do not tithe by estimation"? Rather, Isaac our Patriarch would measure and tithe, but the estimation mentioned in the verse was specifically for the Great Offering. As we learned in the Tractate of Offerings <note>original: *Terumot*, Chapter 1</note>: "We do not give the offering by measure, nor by weight, nor by count." Even though the Sages provided a proportion <note>like the generous eye</note>, it is still legally defined as being given "by estimation." We learn this from the verse: "And your offering shall be reckoned to you," meaning it is like a reckoning or an estimation of the mind. And even though this is written regarding the *tithe of the tithe*, since it is not applicable there <note>because the Torah gave a specific measure of one-tenth for that and it must be measured</note>, apply the rule instead to the Great Offering.

However, if you examine it closely, it implies the estimation was for all tithes. For this estimation preceded the actual growth, as the Sages said: "how much the field was fit to produce." It seems certain that at the time of setting aside the tithe, he would indeed measure it. But the estimation that happened before the crop grew was an act of piety. The law is that one is only obligated to tithe after the processing is finished and the crop enters the home. Isaac’s behavior before that followed the path of complete piety. He wanted to be stringent and would set aside tithes even from what was eaten casually in the field. The rule "Do not tithe by estimation" only applies to the strict legal obligation. But this was a personal stringency of Isaac our Patriarch. And since this verse speaks of the commandment of tithing, it concludes: "And the Lord blessed him." As it is written in the prophet Malachi: "Bring all the tithes into the storehouse... and test Me now in this... if I will not pour out for you a blessing until there is no room to suffice." <note>Malachi 3:10</note> Regarding what I wrote—that they gave the offerings and tithes to Melchizedek—do tithes not belong only to the Levites? Know that Melchizedek was Shem, the son of Noah, and he possessed the power of a Levite according to our tradition. It is said that Aaron the Priest descends from the "kingdom" of Melchizedek. Therefore, Melchizedek represented the "Upper Righteousness" <note>original: *Tzedek Elyon*</note>. Samuel the Prophet, who was a Levite, came from the soul-root of Aaron. This is the hint in the phrase "your brother the Levite." Melchizedek is Shem, and you see that there sat the schools of Shem and Eber... the name "Salem" <note>the root of Jerusalem, meaning "whole"</note> rested upon him. Therefore, Melchizedek's power of voice came from the power of his soul.

### Torah Light

<margin>
Know that the secret of the tithes and the secret of the blessings all go to the same place. Regarding the tithe, the word "blessing" is used. The secret of "finding a hundredfold" also relates to the blessings; our Sages said: "A person is obligated to bless one hundred blessings every day." Regarding the matter of "one hundred gates," Recanati <note>14th-century Italian Kabbalist</note> wrote:
</margin>

And these are his words: "Know that the scholars of Kabbalah said that the Upper Land has one hundred gates. Each gate is a receptacle that flows from the springs of blessing to the world. From there, Isaac our Patriarch drew one hundred kinds of blessings." For the one hundred gates are the seat of the abundance and emanation for all created beings. Therefore, in the Tent of Meeting, there were one hundred sockets <note>term: *Adanim* — the silver bases of the Tabernacle walls</note> for the one hundred talents of silver. Every "land" has a receptacle. I will reveal the secret further: The secret of the tithe <note>original: *Ma'aser*</note> is the number ten, represented by the letter *Yod*. It has three aspects: 1) The *Yod* itself. 2) The "point of the *Yod*" which is a dot, and every dot is a small *Yod*. 3) The "filling" <note>gloss: the way the letter name is spelled out</note> of the *Yod*, which is also ten—the letters *Vav* and *Dalet* of the word *Yod* equal ten. Now, the Emanation <note>term: *Atzilut*</note> consists of nine Sefirot, and the reason it is counted as ten is from the perspective of Wisdom <note>term: *Chokhmah*</note>, as the Name of God hints... as the book *Pardes* <note>Pardes Rimonim by Moshe Cordovero</note> elaborates. The number of Sefirot is from the side of Wisdom, and it "rests in the Crown" <note>term: *Keter*</note> which completes the count. The "point of the *Yod*" hints at the Crown, as the Kabbalists say there are ten Sefirot within Wisdom, and their subtleties are hinted at in the point of the *Yod*, which was hidden. The "filling" of the *Yod* is the expansion of the ten Sefirot, such that each one is comprised of ten. And the divine attribute *Adonai* <note>The Name associated with the Earth/Kingship</note>, which is the secret of the "Upper Land," receives them. These are the secret of the one hundred sockets (*Adanim*). Here you have the secret of the "tithe of the tithe," for in the name *Adonai* there are one hundred gates. They are hidden in Wisdom, which comprises ten. Afterward, they are even more hidden in the ultimate concealment in the point of the *Yod*, until they are glorified in absolute concealment. The *Yod* itself, which is Wisdom, is "carved out" of its point, which is the Crown. This is the secret of one hundred in the expansion of the Emanation and their inclusion of one another. This is the "filling" of the *Yod*. Afterward, they are hidden in their root in Wisdom, which is the essence of the *Yod*. Afterward, they are united in absolute unity in the point of the *Yod*. This is the secret of the tithe and the "tithe of the tithe." Now, the essence of Wisdom is unified with its point, which is the Crown; both are called "Thought" <note>term: *Machshavah*</note>, as we find in many places. See the *Pardes* in the section on terms under the entry "Thought." He writes there in the name of the great Kabbalist Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: "Thought is in the Upper Crown and in Wisdom. In the Upper Crown, it is Thought, but you have no grasp of it at all. Thought precedes all. Wisdom and Understanding come later, and one cannot grasp it at all. Wisdom is also called Thought because it is only grasped through thought, where the beginning of thinking occurs. About these it is said: 'How deep are Your thoughts!' <note>Psalm 92:6</note> For through the 'reckoning' in Wisdom, one comes to think about the Upper Crown." Thus far his words. Now, contemplate the secret of the tithe and the "tithe of the tithe" (the priest's portion of the tithe) and the secret of the Great Offering. This "part" exempts the rest... and is taken by estimation. Every measure is like the hundredfold harvest, in the secret of expansion. The "tithe of the tithe" is the cleaving of the essence to the point of the *Yod*. All of this is fixed in a "measure," for the Emanation is called "Measures" <note>term: *Middot* — referring to the Sefirot as divine qualities</note> which direct all existence. In Wisdom is the root of these measures, and there is the "tithe of the tithe." But the "Great Offering" hints at the essence of the point of the *Yod* itself, which is a level above the cleaving of the essence to its point. For the cleaving of the essence to its point is the cleaving of Wisdom to the Crown, but the point itself is the aspect of the Crown alone. There lies the secret of Thought hidden from thought, through the "estimation of the mind." This is the secret of why the Great Offering is taken by estimation. According to our Sages' ruling on the verse "and it shall be reckoned to you"—meaning in thought and estimation. And even though this verse was written regarding the *tithe of the tithe*, they learned it refers to the Great Offering, where it is taken by estimation. Certainly, what is required by the Torah has a secret as to why it was written here and not in its proper place. And here I say that they hinted at the aforementioned secret: it was written regarding the tithe of the tithe, which is the upper aspect of Wisdom, also called "Thought." This thought cleaves to the power within it, which is "by estimation." Even though this thought is the power of the Great Offering and can be in the Crown—a singular treasure, one out of a hundred—it is nevertheless the aspect of "thoughts toward Thought," which is estimation and not a fixed measure, for it is the root of all measures. And even though it is the number "one" (one out of a hundred), it is a light that is not part of the count, even though it is the head of the count. Therefore, "and it shall be reckoned to you" was written near the tithe of the tithe, even though its subject is the Great Offering. All these things are wondrous.

### And already...

<margin>
For he shall prepare us in the *Tikkunim* <note>The Tikkunei Zohar</note> the secret of "Blessed" (*Barukh*), which is the Holy One, Blessed be He... every one who learns for the sake of the Holy Place...
</margin>

I said that in tithes and blessings there is one secret and one place, as Recanati wrote. To explain the inner secret of the tenth... the secret of the "hundred gates" is explained, as is the secret of "and the Lord blessed him." To explain our "ancient ones" in the "Gates of Light" <note>term: *Sha'arei Orah* — a foundational Kabbalistic text by Joseph Gikatilla</note> in the first gate: the hundred sockets in the Tabernacle are modeled after the one hundred blessings that are filled from the Great Pool <note>original: *Bereichah*, a play on *Berakhah* (blessing)</note> called *Adonai*. Therefore, a person is obligated to bless one hundred blessings every day to draw from each one of the hundreds of blessings. If one is missing, it is a blemish... and he causes a defect in the "Glory of God." This is the secret of the Priest, Levite, and Israelite, which is the secret of the Breath, Spirit, and Soul <note>original: *Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah*</note>. According to this principle, King David said in "Bless the Lord, O my soul," connecting the blessings to the soul through the secret of the three tithes.

Being born from the inner one the outer one,

Of the world, that nevermore is flooded;
